ABOUT HORMEL FOODS — Inspired People. Inspired Food.™

Hormel Foods Corporation, based in Austin, Minnesota, is a global branded food company with approximately $12 billion in annual revenue across more than 80 countries worldwide. Its brands include Planters®, Skippy®, SPAM®, Hormel® Natural Choice®, Applegate®, Justin’s®, Wholly®, Hormel® Black Label®, Columbus®, Jennie-O® and more than 30 other beloved brands. The company is a member of the S&P 500 Index and the S&P 500 Dividend Aristocrats, was named one of the best companies to work for by U.S. News & World Report, one of America’s most responsible companies by Newsweek, recognized by TIME magazine as one of the World’s Best Companies, and has received numerous other awards and accolades for its corporate responsibility and community service efforts. The company lives by its purpose statement — Inspired People. Inspired Food.™ — to bring some of the world’s most trusted and iconic brands to tables across the globe. For more information, visit www.hormelfoods.com.

Hormel Foods Corporation acquired the Planters® and Corn Nuts® businesses in 2021. The Research and Development group for these businesses is based out of a newly renovated space in Northbrook, IL. At this Innovation Center, the team evaluates existing products in addition to creating exciting new products utilizing the labs and pilot plant spaces. The team oversees everything R&D related, from benchtop to full commercialization, including maintenance, NPD, Quality Improvements and cost-saving projects.

Job Purpose: A food packaging intern focuses on the design, development, and improvement of packaging solutions for food products. This role is crucial because packaging affects product safety, shelf life, and consumer appeal.

Responsibilities:

- Involved in one or more of the following assignments:
- Enter data into our packaging specification database system
- Evaluate barrier and abuse characteristics of various packaging materials
- Collaborate with suppliers concerning various packaging systems for our products
- Coordinate "Machine Trial Orders" as part of a label development
- Assist our Packaging Engineers in conducting various abuse tests such as drop, vibration and shipping tests
- Assist in the design of creative packaging options involving point of purchase and Club store displays
- Opportunities to gain knowledge of technical report preparation documenting test results
- Will complete a research project providing experience in true packaging research and development

Requirements:

- Must graduate in August 2027, December 2027, or May 2028 and major in Packaging Engineering with a minimum 3.0 cumulative GPA preferred
- Demonstrated leadership and persuasive skills are necessary for success in this position
- Possess a strong work ethic and an entrepreneurial spirit
- Applicants must not now, or at any time in the future, require employer sponsorship for a work visa
- Applicants must be authorized to work in the United States for any employer
- Must be 18 years of age or older (all plant positions)
- This position will require access to and/or the utilization of a personal motor vehicle to get to and from the workplace
- Must be comfortable with the preparation and consumption of a variety of Hormel Foods Products which may include but not limited to pork, beef, chicken, turkey and nuts

Location and Hours:

- Position is based out of our Research and Development division at our Corporate Office headquarters in Austin MN
- Position is full time, 40 hours per week beginning late May and ending mid-August

Compensation/Benefits:

- Competitive hourly pay of $24.50 paid on a weekly basis
- Housing assistance through either a housing stipend or company-provided housing, depending on location
- Reimbursement of eligible relocation expenses
- Reimbursement for approved business-related expenses
- Opportunity to participate in a 401(k) retirement savings plan with company match
- Paid time off (PTO) accrual
- Hands-on experience with a Fortune 500 company
- Professional development opportunities and networking experiences
- Potential consideration for future internships, co-ops, or full-time employment opportunities

How We Work At Chick-fil-A

Chick-fil-A, Inc. ('Chick-fil-A' or 'the Company') Staff members play a vital role in achieving our strategic goals by developing their skills, fostering inclusive teamwork, and embracing innovation. All Staff are expected to contribute to a compelling future by inspiring and motivating those around them. Growth and development are essential at Chick-fil-A. We want Staff to seek new perspectives and adopt new methods to drive continuous improvement and adaptation to evolving business needs. Lastly, we ask Staff to seek wisdom, expect the best, accept responsibility, respond with courage, and think others first.

Our Flexible Futures Model offers a healthy mix of working in person (currently a minimum of 8-10 days per month) and virtually, strengthening key elements of the Chick-fil-A culture by fostering collaboration and community.
Overview

The DTT Co-Op Program offers participants a unique environment to learn Chick-fil-A’s business, culture, and technology in a safe and supportive environment. The program is committed to developing participants personally and professionally through hands-on experience, workshops, mentorship, and project work. Participants have the opportunity to explore both technical and functional tracks, enabling cross-functional skill development. This is a 3 semester Co-Op operating on a non-sequential, every-other-semester, basis. The 1st semester is the Foundations semester for Co-Ops where participants will gain hands-on learning and project experience. The 2nd and 3rd semesters are apprenticeship semesters where Co-Ops are embedded into a team alongside a coach. Co-Ops will rotate college coursework between each semester they serve with Chick-fil-A, Inc. The DTT Co-Op is a separate program from Chick-fil-A’s traditional, summer internship program.

- This is a paid opportunity
- Only full-time opportunities are available (Co-Ops are encouraged to not take coursework while working) [TM1.1]
- Must commit to working 3 semesters for Chick-fil-A
- Must have at least 3 semesters of college coursework remaining before graduation and must be pursuing an undergraduate degree in a technical field

Hiring for both Technical and Functional roles.

C1 (first semester of the Co-Op): All DTT C1s complete a 4-5 week bootcamp, upskilling them on relevant skills to help them succeed in project work. C1s serve on teams together to complete two different projects for the remainder of the semester. Possibility to serve in both technical and functional capacities.

C2 (second semester of the Co-Op): Co-Ops are assigned to a project team based on their interest, project impact, business objectives, and team needs. At this stage, Co-Ops select either the engineer or analyst track. Co-Ops are embedded onto an existing project team and contribute directly to that team’s goals and initiatives. All teams in our department are eligible to request a Co-Op, so any Chick-fil-A technology is a candidate for a Co-Op project. Function as a junior career member of the team.

C3 (third semester of the Co-Op): Option to remain on current team or try something new. It is virtually the same as C2. Participants are partnered with an Early Talent Coach to support their initiatives. Function as a junior career member of the team.

The Digital Transformation & Technology (DTT) Co-Op will have the opportunity to:

- Leverage cloud technologies to build reliable, scalable, and maintainable products
- Develop proficiency in programming languages such as Java, JavaScript, Python, and Go
- Build impactful technology that serves staff, customers, operators, or team members.
- Cultivate relationships across technical and functional peers and Chick-fil-A Technology leadership
- Solve business critical problems by serving on a team to build innovative solutions

Participants are paired with an Early Talent Coach for the duration of each semester. Early Talent Coaches are a Co-Op's go-to resource for support, work direction, and input.

This program gives participants the opportunity to leverage programming and project management skills in a real-life working environment. Participants get to experience first-hand Chick-fil-A’s corporate culture and participate in a range of DTT projects. Participants are presented with leadership opportunities while gaining key skills and perspective necessary for a successful career in DTT at Chick-fil-A, Inc. or in DTT more broadly. To see some of the exciting work the technology team is engaged in, visit our Medium Blog.

Responsibilities

Previous Project Examples:

- Invoice Routing Automation in the cloud
- Full-stack web app to search and filter APIs
- Develop features for IoT devices in the restaurant
- Strategize and execute plan to enhance the Chick-fil-A customer experience
- Support digital workplace transformation for Corporate Staff

Job Responsibilities & Activities:

- Learn about a variety Chick-fil-A systems and technologies
- Contribute to current DTT projects or initiatives with guidance from an Early Talent Coach
- Influence new and innovative ways to solve current business and technical challenges
- Hear from key members of the DTT department to better understand DTT roles and key functions
- Understand Chick-fil-A systems, technologies, and best practices
- Grow technical skills in a variety of domains
- Deepen knowledge of Chick-fil-A history and culture through programmatic experiences

During project(s) Co-Ops are responsible to:

- Deliver project outcomes with support from an Early Talent Coach
- Contribute working software to an agile team
- Leverage resources and skills to contribute meaningfully to a project
- Drive results to meet project timelines
- Tell the story of the potential impact of a project
- Receive guidance on DTT projects or initiatives from an Early Talent coach
- Learn from key members of the DTT department to better understand technology roles and key functions
- Grow in professionalism, executive presence, personal branding, design thinking, and team collaboration

Assignments may include but are not limited to the following:

- Investigate new technologies and services
- Design, develop, and deploy software solutions
- Build technical solutions for Chick-fil-A Restaurants, Corporate Staff, or Customers
- Present solutions to key stakeholders

Required Qualifications (Knowledge, Skills, & Abilities)

- The Co-Op program requires a commitment to three non-consecutive work rotations. You must be available to work during the following periods:

- Rotation 1 (Spring): Jan 11, 2027 – April 30, 2027 (16 weeks)
- Rotation 2 (Summer): May 17, 2027 – July 30, 2027 (11 weeks)
- Rotation 3 (Fall): Aug 23, 2027 – Dec 10, 2027 (16 weeks)

- Actively pursuing an undergraduate degree in Computer Science, Computer Engineering, CIS, MIS, Industrial Engineering, HCI, Software Engineering, Computational Media, or other related technical major
- Strong analytical and problem-solving skills
- Excellent communication skills
- Excellent interpersonal and team collaboration skills
- 3 semesters minimum of college coursework remaining
- Interest in long-term career trajectory in a technical field
- Demonstrated creative problem solving, leadership, and strong
- communication skills through class projects, jobs, clubs, and/or internships

0%

High School Diploma or GED

No

The Department of Environmental Services (DES) is seeking an Utility Engineering Intern will assist the Water Sewer Streets Bureau in managing the maintenance and capital planning of 1,058 lane miles of street, 443 miles of sidewalk, 525 miles of water mains, 458 miles of sanitary sewer mains, 373 miles of stormwater mains and associated structures such as manholes, catch basins, and outfalls.

Responsibilities

Major Job Duties:

- Supporting routine field inspections of water, sanitary sewer, and stormwater infrastructure, including water mains, storm and sanitary sewer mains, valves, hydrants, manholes, and storm drains;
- Documenting field conditions through photographs, field notes, and asset management systems (AMS);
- Conducting engineering records research to verify and update asset management data for water, sewer, and transportation assets, including mains, manholes, hydrants, valves, guardrails, and retaining walls;
- Utilizing ArcGIS Pro, Cartegraph, Microsoft Excel, Power BI, and other software applications to generate reports, analyze and visualize data, create maps, and identify recurring asset maintenance issues;
- Preparing as-built documentation and updating engineering record drawings using Adobe software;
- Assisting with tracking Supervisory Control and Data Acquisition (SCADA) system data to identify unusual operating conditions for staff review;
- Organizing project files, maps, and documentation to support operations and maintenance activities; and
- Performing other duties as assigned.

Location: Trades Center, 4200 28th Street S. Arlington, VA 22206
Arlington County

Arlington County is an innovative local government in Northern Virginia seeking motivated candidates for one-year internship opportunities across multiple departments. These roles are ideal for recent graduates and current graduate students with limited professional experience who are looking to kickstart their careers.

Interns gain hands-on experience supporting key County initiatives while participating in a structured cohort-based development program. Throughout the year, interns work under the mentorship of senior staff, contributing fresh ideas, improving processes, and leveraging technology to enhance organizational effectiveness, all while familiarizing themselves with a public-sector environment.

Qualifications

Minimum Qualifications: Recent, 2025 and/or 2026 college graduates earning either a Bachelor’s or a Master’s degree* in the area of consideration prior to the start date of the Cohort Program (Sept. 2026) must have:

- No professional-level work experience (less than one year) in the internship field; and
- You may be a currently enrolled student in a Master’s degree program related to the internship, but you must not have significant professional-level work experience in the internship area and must be available to work during designated hours.

Degree Requirements: Civil Engineering, Environmental Engineering, Data Science Engineering, Computer Science, Chemical Engineering, Mechanical Engineering, Statistics, Economics, or related discipline.

Desirable Qualifications: Preference may be given to applicants with one or more of the following:

- G.P.A. of 3.0 or above is preferred and applicants may be asked to provide certified official transcripts;
- Proficiency in Microsoft Office programs (Excel, Word, PowerPoint, SharePoint, Teams, PowerBI, etc.);
- Familiarity with Cartegraph or similar asset management software;
- Familiarity with ESRI (GIS) software;
- Familiarity with Adobe software; and/or
- Experience with data analysis and asset management.

Special Requirements

Background Check: A pre-employment criminal records check will be conducted. It will include checks of the following: criminal record, driving record, education, professional licensure, and credit history. You will be required to sign a release authorizing the County to obtain your background information.

Driver's License: Applicant must possess, or obtain by time of appointment, a valid driver’s license, and must provide or authorize Arlington County to obtain a copy of official driving record. Any offer of employment may be contingent upon favorable review of the applicant’s driving record. Alternatively, the applicant must have the ability and willingness to use alternative methods of transportation to perform assigned duties and responsibilities at locations other than the primary worksite.

Please complete each section of the application including the supplemental questions. Your responses to the supplemental questions are required because they provide us with specific information necessary to evaluate your qualifications for this position. These responses are considered part of the selection process. A resume may be attached; however, it will not substitute for a completed application. Incomplete applications will not be considered. Please do not write "see resume" as a response to the questions.

Additional Information

Work hours: Core work hours are between 8:00 a.m. to 5:00 p.m., Monday through Friday. This is not a fully remote opportunity. Employees will be expected to be in the office at the discretion of the Supervisor and needs of the agency as well as to attend in-person classroom training.

Applicants may be asked to provide certified official transcripts.

All Cohort Interns are eligible for County government employee benefits that include health, dental and leave.

Business Unit / Role Specific Info

The Enterprise Technology Services organization partners with every part of the American Express business to power the company’s growth and innovation with trust and efficiency, and drive competitive differentiation with speed. We support the delivery and operations of technology, digital, and data capabilities, platforms, and services globally. Specifically, our team is responsible for the company’s technology engineering, architecture, and infrastructure, providing 24x7 support to ensure an uninterrupted, high-quality experience for customers and colleagues. We also provide product management for core enterprise platforms, and lead technology risk and information security, enterprise data governance and platforms, digital product and design, and enterprise AI platforms on behalf of the company.

At American Express, we empower future technologists to learn, innovate, and make an impact from day one. As an Associate Digital Product Management Intern in Enterprise Technology Services, you’ll join a 10-week Summer Internship Program and contribute to product, platform, and delivery initiatives that help shape seamless customer and colleague experiences.

Product Management interns sit at the intersection of business, technology, data, design, delivery, and customer experience. In this role, you’ll help teams understand customer needs, document requirements, prioritize work, track delivery outcomes, manage risks and dependencies, and support Agile planning activities that help technology teams deliver value responsibly and at enterprise scale.

You’ll collaborate with Product Managers, Engineers, Designers, Data Analysts, Architects, Delivery Leads, and business partners to learn how products and technology initiatives are envisioned, built, launched, measured, governed, and continuously improved.

About the Team

Enterprise Technology Services teams build and support technology that enables trusted, secure, and customer-first experiences across American Express. Product and delivery teams help define strategy, prioritize investments, coordinate execution, and improve delivery practices across digital products, platforms, internal tools, developer experiences, AI enabled capabilities, and enterprise technology solutions.

As a Product Management Intern, you’ll contribute at an early-career level while learning how modern product teams balance customer needs, business outcomes, technical feasibility, delivery execution, operational resilience, and responsible innovation.

Responsibilities

What type of work can you expect? How will you make an impact in this role?

- Support Product Managers and delivery teams in defining, refining, and prioritizing product requirements, features, user stories, acceptance criteria, and support documentation.
- Assist with customer discovery, stakeholder interviews, user research activities, usability testing, and analysis of feedback to help inform product decisions.
- Collaborate with engineering, design, analytics, risk, security, operations, and business teams to support product delivery and technology initiatives.
- Support Agile Release Train, backlog refinement, sprint planning, demos, retrospectives, and other Agile ceremonies with guidance from peers and leaders.
- Monitor risks, dependencies, capacity considerations, and impediments to delivery; escalate issues that may require decisions or support from senior product, delivery, or engineering leaders.
- Facilitate or document technical discussions related to architectural approach, system design, roadmap tradeoffs, delivery readiness, and implementation planning.
- Create, consolidate, and analyze portfolio, release train, product, and team-level metrics to provide insights into delivery progress, execution quality, risks, and key decisions needed.
- Support product and engineering teams in building implementation roadmaps, managing cross-functional dependencies, and preparing leadership updates on delivery status.
- Identify opportunities to improve delivery processes, redesign process flows, strengthen documentation practices, and support continuous learning across teams.

Qualifications

Minimum Qualifications

- Currently enrolled in a full-time Bachelor’s degree program (software engineering, business, MIS, Business Analytics).
- Demonstrated interest in technology, product management, digital products, customer experience, Agile delivery, or technology program delivery.
- Strong analytical and problem-solving skills with the ability to evaluate information, identify patterns, and distill complex topics into clear recommendations.
- Strong written and verbal communication skills with the ability to explain ideas clearly and concisely.
- Ability to collaborate effectively in a team environment and build relationships with cross-functional partners.
- Familiarity with customer journeys, user-centered design, feature prioritization, product strategy, roadmap planning, requirements definition, user stories, and launch readiness.

Public Investments – Quantitative Analyst Internship (undergraduate-level)

Job Description

Northwestern Mutual's Public Investment Department seeks a Quantitative Analyst Intern to join us for the summer of 2027 and play a pivotal role in building out tools and conducting analyses that help shape our investment processes. We manage over $130 billion in fixed income assets, and you will collaborate directly with Portfolio Managers, Traders, and Credit Analysts to develop cutting-edge solutions.

Principal Responsibilities:

You'll have the opportunity to leverage your unique strengths and interests within a flexible role that spans data, modeling, visualization, and applications. Your activities will center around driving investment performance through innovative improvements to our investment processes, such as relative value analysis, portfolio construction, trading tools, risk measurement, and more.

- Build & maintain data models: Collaborate with data engineers to onboard new data sources, design and implement dbt SQL models for data cleaning and integration, and write robust data quality tests to ensure data integrity.
- Develop interactive data visualizations: Create insightful dashboards and applications using Tableau and Streamlit to effectively communicate data and model outputs to the department’s investment professionals.
- Design and implement machine learning models: Utilize machine learning and AI techniques to develop predictive models, optimize model parameters, research new signals, and deploy models into the Snowflake production environment.
- Apply quantitative methods: Leverage quantitative methods such as portfolio optimization, Monte Carlo simulation, risk measurement, and backtesting to enhance various aspects of the investment process.
- Collaborate effectively: Work closely with Portfolio Managers, Traders, and Credit Analysts to better identify attractive investment opportunities through efficient data delivery, advanced models, and intuitive dashboards.

Job Requirements:

- Progress towards a Bachelor’s degree in a quantitative field (e.g., Quantitative Finance, Computer/Data Science, Finance, Mathematics).
- Strong development skills in languages such as SQL, Python, Streamlit, dbt, etc.
- Excellent data manipulation and data visualization skills.
- Experience with software development practices such as version control and CI/CD pipelines is preferred.
- Experience using Bloomberg and BlackRock Aladdin is a plus.

Interpersonal Skills

- Passion for the art and science of investing.
- Effective oral and written communication skills.
- Demonstrated analytical and problem-solving ability.
- High degree of self-motivation, passion, and a drive to learn.

About the Internship Program
Internship candidates can expect a fulltime onsite internship program, running from June 2027 to August 2027. Carefully selected from universities across the country, our interns bring distinctive ideas and perspectives to our organization. Our employees are passionate about building our emerging talent and future leaders. In addition to their day-to-day tasks, interns participate in professional development workshops, senior leadership Q&A's, volunteer initiatives, networking/social events, and more!

About the Public Investment Department

Northwestern Mutual’s Public Investments Department manages over $130 billion in investment grade and high yield fixed income assets backing NM’s General Account insurance products and retirement plan assets, and oversees about half of the company’s total General Account assets. The team actively manages these assets with a goal of generating long-run total returns in excess of benchmarks to drive policyholder value. This role will be within the Quantitative Research & Analytics team.

JOB DESCRIPTION AND POSITION REQUIREMENTS

We are searching for a motivated undergraduate student to join the Visualization and Decision Support Division at the Applied Research Laboratory (ARL) at Penn State. This fall/spring internship will concentrate on gaining hands-on experience in AI/ML data preparation and contributing to meaningful research

ARL is an authorized DoD SkillBridge partner and welcomes all transitioning military members to apply.

Typical focus areas include:

- Label and annotate diverse datasets with a primary focus on geospatial data such as tracks, images, video, text, and sensor data
- Support AI/ML model development for Navy, Department of Defense (DoD), and Intelligence Community (IC) applications
- Utilize industry-standard and custom labeling tools while collaborating with AI/ML researchers and engineers to understand requirements and contribute to data quality assurance processes

Students majoring in the following fields are encouraged to apply:

- Undergraduate students in a STEM major (Computer Science, Engineering, Mathematics, Data Science, Information Sciences, or related fields)

Interest Skills/Experience areas include:

- Drive to learn and grow in the AI/ML field
- Commitment to data quality
- Strong attention to detail

Preferred but not required:

- Interest in artificial intelligence, machine learning, or data science
- Familiarity with geospatial concepts or mapping technologies
- Previous experience with data analysis or annotation at any level

You will work up to 20 hours/week during the fall and spring semesters and have the opportunity to work up to 40 hours/week over the summer. This is a paid internship opportunity, and location will be fully on-site located in State College, PA

Relocation and housing are not provided. Questions related to flexible work should be directed to the hiring manager during the interview process.

ARL’s purpose is to research and develop innovative solutions to challenging scientific, engineering, and technology problems in support of the Navy, the Intel Community (IC), and other federal government customers.
